Topics: Reading Literature - Interactions Among Text Elements
SubTopics: Analyze how particular elements of a text interact including how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.
Content: How does the passage's setting affect the plot?

A.Choice: Being outside helps Rebecca to relax despite her concerns about leaving home.

B.Choice: Being in the treehouse makes Rebecca consider what she will miss after moving away.

C.Choice: Being alone with her father leads Rebecca to confess her frustration with her mother's actions.

D.Choice: Being around her sketchbooks causes Rebecca to question whether she should pursue architecture.

Topics: Reading Literature - Close Reading Of Text
SubTopics: Cite several pieces of textual evidence and make relevant connections to support analysis of what a literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
Content: This question has `bbtext(two)` parts. First, answer Part A. Then, answer Part B.
Which sentence describes Rebecca and her father?

D.Choice: They share a dream for the future.

Content: Select `bbtext(two)` sentences from the passage that support the answer in Part A.

A.Choice: “The only change in our fifteen-year tradition had been to swap our old, dark tent for a newly built treehouse . . .” (paragraph 1)

B.Choice: “I woke this morning to Dad waving the remains of our half-eaten bag of Cheetos under my nose.” (paragraph 2)

C.Choice: “Ninety-nine percent of the time, I agreed with Dad, but on the topic of my treehouse, we disagreed.” (paragraph 5)

D.Choice: “I cleared my throat to ward off the threat of tears and managed a wry smile for my father.” (paragraph 6)

E.Choice: “'No offense, but I would have been more excited if I was going to college by myself.'” (paragraph 6)

Topics: Reading Literature - Perspective & Purpose In Texts
SubTopics: Determine how an author conveys or develops perspective or purpose in a text through contrasting the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.
Content: How does the author contrast Rebecca's and her father's points of view?

A.Choice: by showing that Rebecca feels guilty for wanting to be far from her parents while her father wishes they could be closer

B.Choice: by showing that Rebecca's father wants to continue their camping tradition while Rebecca is less concerned about the change

C.Choice: by showing how Rebecca thinks her father wants to move but then revealing that he would actually prefer to remain in their current house

D.Choice: by showing that Rebecca's father understands that Rebecca wants independence but underestimates how much she will miss her current house

Which theme is developed in the passage?

A.Choice: Leaving the familiar behind can make a person sad.

B.Choice: Accepting family members as they are can be a relief.

C.Choice: Students can be proud after setting and achieving a goal.

D.Choice: People should rely on others for help in challenging times.

Content: Which sentence from the passage helps to develop the theme in Part A?

A.Choice: “It probably sounds stupid, but we hadn't even moved and I was already homesick for this tiny nest that housed all my architecture books and sketchbooks.” (paragraph 5)

B.Choice: “And best of all, the models I'd constructed at the summer camp I attended two years ago through the architecture school at the University of Washington . . .” (paragraph 5)

C.Choice: “'At least I talked your mom into moving to New Jersey instead of New York.'” (paragraph 8)

D.Choice: “'You have no idea how much I appreciate that,' I said fervently . . .” (paragraph 9)
